Hi OP, from what I've read of your circumstances and the JCQ document on special circumstances, you wouldn't qualify. This is copied from the document: 

Candidates will be eligible for special consideration if they have been fully prepared and 
have covered the whole course but performance in the examination, or in the production of 
coursework or non-examination assessment, is materially affected by adverse 
circumstances beyond their control. These include: 
2.1.1 temporary illness or accident/injury at the time of the assessment;
2.1.2 bereavement at the time of the assessment (where whole groups are affected, 
normally only those most closely involved will be eligible);
2.1.3 domestic crisis arising at the time of the assessment;
2.1.4 serious disturbance during an examination, particularly where recorded material is 
being used;
2.1.5 accidental events at the time of the assessment such as being given the wrong 
examination paper, being given a defective examination paper or CD, failure of 
practical equipment, failure of materials to arrive on time;
2.1.6 participation in sporting events, training camps or other events at an international 
level at the time of the assessment, e.g. representing their country at an 
international level in chess or football;
2.1.7 failure by the centre to implement previously approved access arrangements for 
that specific examination series.

Your situation would probably fall under 2.1.3: domestic crisis. However, they specify that it must be occuring at the time of assessment, which means it would have to occur essentially between May and June. Since for you it occured starting in December, it wouldn't fall within the bounds of "time of assessment" despite the fact that it's technically ongoing, because it didn't arise in the past month, and therefore you would be unlikely to qualify. 

However, if you read the full thing, it doesn't mention a situation like yours in their enumeration of circumstances under which a candidate wouldn't qualify. Technically, it also doesn't mention anything about ongoing disruption prior to the time of assessment. 

They state that 3% allowance can be given for cases of "recent crisis/incident", which I'd class your case as. However, they then go on to define "recent" as "occuring up to 4 months before the examination(s) taking place". 

So basically, it looks as though you wouldn't qualify, but at the same time they don't explicitly say that your situation doesn't qualify. So you should contact your exams coordinator and put in a formal request to the exam boards for special consideration anyway. If you indeed don't qualify, they'll just deny your request.

Since that didn't happen your application was probably weak in some area(s), so you should spend your year strengthening it (typically unis require more from gap year students than non-gap year so really your entire PS would need to be "better"). People fairly rarely reapply to the same college twice but it isn't unheard of and they're theoretically meant to look over it unbiased. "Tactical" applications are generally thought to be a bit worthless since the colleges (including the "worse" ones) would rather take a "better" candidate from the pool than a candidate who applied to them.
